You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

(105) General-purpose AI models, in particular large generative AI models, capable of generating text, images, and other content, present unique innovation opportunities but also challenges to artists, authors, and other creators and the way their creative content is created, distributed, used and consumed. The development and training of such models require access to vast amounts of text, images, videos and other data. Text and data mining techniques may be used extensively in this context for the retrieval and analysis of such content, which may be protected by copyright and related rights. Any use of copyright protected content requires the authorisation of the rightsholder concerned unless relevant copyright exceptions and limitations apply. Directive (EU) 2019/790 introduced exceptions and limitations allowing reproductions and extractions of works or other subject matter, for the purpose of text and data mining, under certain conditions. Under these rules, rightsholders may choose to reserve their rights over their works or other subject matter to prevent text and data mining, unless this is done for the purposes of scientific research. Where the rights to opt out has been expressly reserved in an appropriate manner, providers of general-purpose AI models need to obtain an authorisation from rightsholders if they want to carry out text and data mining over such works.

(Testo Unico), articolo 71, in virtù del quale il datore di lavoro deve, non solo mettere a disposizione dei lavoratori attrezzature conformi ai requisiti di sicurezza, conformemente alle disposizioni legislative nazionali o di recepimento delle direttive comunitarie e adeguate al lavoro da svolgere ma deve anche provvedere affinché tali attrezzature siano oggetto di idonea manutenzione al fine di garantire nel tempo la rispondenza alle caratteristiche tecniche e di funzionamento originali. L’obbligo della manutenzione è applicabile a tutte le attrezzature di lavoro, nessuna esclusa. Per particolari attrezzature, il cui utilizzo comporta pericoli particolari e riportate nell’Allegato VII del T.U. e ss.mm.ii., occorre eseguire verifiche periodiche con una periodicità stabilita dal legislatore da parte di personale specializzato dell’ASP di competenza o Organismo privato riconosciuto. In appendice vengono riportati in forma integrale gli articoli 69, 70, 71 del D. Lgs. 81/08, nonché l’Allegato VII del medesimo decreto. Ogni attrezzatura e macchina dovrà essere sottoposta a un regime di verifiche e di manutenzione specifico, essenzialmente sulla base delle prescrizioni del fabbricante e di eventuali leggi specifiche, come ad esempio nel caso delle gru, dei trattori agricoli-forestali, delle piattaforme elevatrici, etc.. La dimostrabilità dell’avvenuta manutenzione avviene attraverso documentazione che attesti gli interventi eseguiti sulle attrezzature (ad intervalli prefissati o al guasto) e l’eventuale sostituzione di parti o dispositivi con ricambi idonei.
